summary: Altretamine (hexamethylmelamine) is an oral cytotoxic agent used as a single agent for the palliative treatment of persistent or recurrent ovarian cancer after first-line therapy with a cisplatin- or alkylating-agent-based combination. The recommended dose is 260 mg/m2/day given in four divided doses, for either 14 or 21 consecutive days of a 28-day cycle. Its two principal dose-limiting toxicities are myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia) and neurotoxicity (peripheral sensory neuropathy and central effects such as mood changes and ataxia). It can cause severe orthostatic hypotension when combined with monoamine oxidase inhibitors. Complete blood counts and neurologic examinations are required before and periodically during therapy.
indications: Single-agent palliative treatment of patients with persistent or recurrent ovarian cancer following first-line therapy with a cisplatin- or alkylating-agent-based combination

moa: The precise mechanism of altretamine's antitumor activity is unknown. Although structurally related to the alkylating agent triethylenemelamine (TEM), it does not act as a classical alkylating agent in standard assays. Its cytotoxicity may involve metabolic activation by hepatic microsomal enzymes to reactive intermediates that damage tumor DNA, possibly through the formation of DNA-protein and DNA-DNA cross-links. Antitumor activity has been demonstrated in ovarian carcinoma.

preg: Altretamine can cause fetal harm; it was teratogenic and embryotoxic in animals. It should not be used in pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should avoid becoming pregnant and use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: It is not known whether altretamine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a nursing infant from a cytotoxic drug, breastfeeding should be discontinued during therapy.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; monitor renal function and for accumulation of toxicity. Dose modification may be required if significant impairment develops.
hepatic: Altretamine undergoes extensive hepatic metabolism; use with caution and monitor in hepatic impairment, with attention to enhanced toxicity.

missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume your usual schedule. Do not take a double dose. Tell your doctor if you miss several doses.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose would be expected to intensify the principal toxicities - severe myelosuppression and neurotoxicity, with nausea and vomiting. Discontinue the drug and provide supportive care, including blood-count monitoring and transfusion or growth-factor support as needed for marrow suppression.
